title: seedObligations does not validate per-user deposit >= MINIMUM_STAKE, allowing a single non-conforming entry to permanently brick migrateDeposits
description: `MigratorV1V2.seedObligations` accepts an array of per-user `_deposits` without checking that each non-zero deposit is at least `MINIMUM_STAKE` (1e15). `migrateDeposits` later iterates the user list and calls `phlimboV2.stake(dep, users[i])` for any user where `dep > 0`. `PhlimboV2.stake` enforces `require(amount >= MINIMUM_STAKE, "Below minimum stake")`. If any seeded deposit is in the range (0, MINIMUM_STAKE), the call reverts inside the loop, reverting the entire `migrateDeposits` transaction. Because `seedObligations` is one-shot (`require(!seeded)` is permanent), there is no in-contract path to remove or correct the offending entry. The owner can only `withdrawAll()` to recover funds, leaving the migration permanently incomplete.
impact: A single misconfigured deposit value (off-chain snapshot error, V1 user with a sub-minimum residual position, etc.) permanently bricks the on-chain migration path for ALL downstream users in the iteration order. The owner cannot re-seed, cannot skip individual users, and cannot adjust the deposit values. Recovery requires deploying a new migrator contract, re-funding it, and likely re-granting V2's `setMigrator` and the phUSD mint role — operationally expensive and creates a window where two migrators coexist. The same concern applies to V1's MINIMUM_STAKE history: V1 also enforces a minimum stake, but if MINIMUM_STAKE was ever changed between V1 and V2, or if V1 had any historical edge case allowing sub-minimum balances, this issue triggers.
exploitScenario:
1. Owner takes an off-chain snapshot of V1 stakers. One user, due to a V1 dust-prevention edge case (or an off-chain script bug, or a hand-edited deposit value), has `deposit = 5e14` (below MINIMUM_STAKE = 1e15).
2. Owner calls `seedObligations` with this user's entry in the array. The call succeeds because no per-user minimum is enforced.
3. Owner funds the contract with `totalPHUSD_deposited` phUSD and `totalUSDC` USDC.
4. Owner calls `settleDebt(maxIterations)` to completion — succeeds (no MINIMUM_STAKE check in settle).
5. Owner calls `migrateDeposits(maxIterations)`. The loop reaches the offending user, calls `phlimboV2.stake(5e14, user)`, which reverts with 'Below minimum stake'. The entire migrateDeposits transaction reverts. The contract's `migrateIterator` remains pointing to (or before) the offending index.
6. Any retry with `maxIterations >= 1` reverts at the same index. There is no per-user skip mechanism.
7. Owner is forced to call `withdrawAll()` to recover phUSD, deploy a new migrator (sans the offending entry), re-execute the wirings (phUSD mint role, V2 setMigrator), and restart migration for the remaining users. Meanwhile the offending user's V1 deposit is effectively unmigrable through this contract.
recommendation: Add a per-element validation in the `seedObligations` loop: `require(_deposits[i] == 0 || _deposits[i] >= MINIMUM_STAKE, "Deposit below minimum stake");` (reading MINIMUM_STAKE from `phlimboV2.MINIMUM_STAKE()` to stay in sync). Alternatively, in `migrateDeposits` add a per-iteration skip: `if (dep > 0 && dep < phlimboV2.MINIMUM_STAKE()) { /* skip with event */ continue; }` so the loop tolerates non-conforming entries. The first option is preferable because it surfaces the misconfiguration at seed time rather than after funds are committed. Either fix should also be added to `seedObligations`' length checks and any future migration variants.
dedup_reasoning: Standalone migrator finding: missing MINIMUM_STAKE validation in seedObligations bricks downstream migrateDeposits with no on-chain remediation. Distinct from H-02 (V1 drain enforcement), M-03 (auto-claim of pre-existing V2 position), and M-04 (strict balance equality grief). No overlap in root cause or fix.
sanitize_reasoning: Not covered by any documented design decision or known issue. V1 enforces the same MINIMUM_STAKE so in practice V1 snapshots should not contain sub-minimum deposits, but the migrator code itself contains no defensive check and seedObligations is one-shot. The brick-on-revert behavior with no on-chain skip and a recovery that requires full redeploy is a legitimate code-design concern. Note: arguably 'reckless admin mistake' if the snapshot script is at fault, but the contract's one-shot seeding + strict-equality balance gates leave the owner without an in-contract fix path, which elevates this above pure operator-error. Keep at medium.
rejection_reason: Falls under C4 'reckless admin mistake' known-invalid. Phlimbo V1 enforces the same MINIMUM_STAKE = 1e15 on stake() (Phlimbo.sol:296) and has explicit dust prevention on withdraw (Phlimbo.sol:346-351) that forces full withdrawal if remaining lands in (0, MINIMUM_STAKE). Therefore V1 on-chain state cannot contain a balance in the (0, MINIMUM_STAKE) range. The bug can only manifest if the owner manually fabricates a sub-minimum value when seeding - pure admin authorship error, no untrusted-attacker path, no external requirement. PoC proves the brick mechanic but not a non-admin path to the malformed input. The finding's own metadata already flagged it as 'borderline:medium-defensible.' Independent validity-checker and severity-auditor both recommended rejection or QA downgrade.
classification_reasoning: C4 audit-mode Medium: 'protocol function or availability impacted, or value leak with stated assumptions.' Stated assumption: any single seeded deposit falls below MINIMUM_STAKE. External requirement: the snapshot includes at least one sub-minimum entry (possible from V1 historical edge cases or off-chain script error). Impact: protocol function (migration availability) permanently impaired with no on-chain recovery path; user funds are not stolen but the migration path is bricked, requiring full migrator redeploy and re-wiring of mint roles and setMigrator. Does not meet High because the funds remain recoverable via owner withdrawAll + redeploy, but availability of the migration path is a clear protocol-function impact.
validity_check: borderline: brushes the 'reckless admin' line because the trigger is an off-chain snapshot error, but the contract design (one-shot seedObligations + strict balance equality gates + no per-user skip) leaves the owner with zero in-contract remediation. C4 has accepted similar 'one-shot configuration with no recovery path' issues as Medium. The sub-minimum case is plausible (V1 enforces the same minimum but historical edge cases or dust-prevention logic could produce sub-minimum residuals). Keep as valid Medium; sponsor may close as 'mitigated by snapshot validation,' which is a fair outcome but does not invalidate the finding.
severity_audit_reasoning: Independent assessment: Medium is defensible but contested in both directions. Argument for LOW/QA: V1 enforces MINIMUM_STAKE on stake (Phlimbo.sol L296) AND has dust-prevention on withdraw (L346-348), so V1 cannot naturally produce sub-minimum entries. The only realistic trigger is an off-chain snapshot script bug, which brushes 'reckless admin mistake' territory (C4 invalid). Argument for MEDIUM: The contract's one-shot seedObligations + strict-equality balance gates + no per-user skip mechanism elevate a single recoverable input error into a full redeploy with role re-wiring — that is a code-design brittleness concern, not pure operator error. The contract makes no defensive check against a foreseeable input class. Audit-mode Medium template fits: 'protocol function or availability impacted, with stated assumptions and external requirements.' Stated assumption: sub-minimum seed entry exists. External requirement: snapshot misconfiguration. NOT upgrading to High (funds remain recoverable via withdrawAll; the impact is availability, not loss). NOT downgrading to Low because the brick semantics and lack of on-chain recovery elevate this above a documentation/hardening fix. Defensible center is Medium. Sponsor may legitimately close as 'will validate snapshot off-chain' — that does not invalidate the finding's code-design observation. Worth noting in submission that this is borderline; consider explicit language acknowledging the snapshot-validation mitigation as part of the recommendation.
